test_prompts.name: single-url-python-audit
test_prompts.prompt: Write a python script that runs a Lighthouse audit on a single URL. The script should use a headless desktop configuration and verify that the Performance, Accessibility, and SEO scores are all above 90. If any score is below 90, it should exit with a non-zero status code.
test_prompts.expected_output: A complete Python script that runs npx lighthouse via subprocess, parses the JSON report, extracts scores, validates them, and exits appropriately.
evaluation_criteria: Produces a valid, self-contained Python script
Uses subprocess to run 'npx lighthouse' with headless Chrome flags
Includes the '--preset=desktop' CLI argument
Parses the resulting JSON report file to extract category scores
Includes assertions for performance, accessibility, and SEO scores against a threshold of 90
Exits with sys.exit(1) or raises an error when assertions fail

test_prompts.name: robot-framework-integration
test_prompts.prompt: We want to run Lighthouse audits as part of our Robot Framework test suite. Write a .robot file and a supporting Python library LighthouseLibrary.py containing keywords to run audits and assert scores and Web Vitals (LCP < 2500ms, CLS < 0.1).
test_prompts.expected_output: A Robot Framework .robot suite file and a LighthouseLibrary.py file containing custom Python keywords.
evaluation_criteria: Produces a valid .robot file utilizing a custom library LighthouseLibrary
Produces a valid LighthouseLibrary.py defining keywords like 'Run Lighthouse Audit' and assertion keywords
The Python library runs the Lighthouse CLI and parses the JSON report
Includes assertions checking that LCP is under 2500ms
Includes assertions checking that CLS is under 0.1

test_prompts.name: lighthouse-ci-config
test_prompts.prompt: Create a configuration template for Lighthouse CI (lighthouserc.json) and a GitHub Actions workflow to run audits on the URL https://staging.example.com on every push.
test_prompts.expected_output: A valid lighthouserc.json configuration and a GitHub Actions workflow YAML file.
evaluation_criteria: Produces a valid JSON lighthouserc.json structure
lighthouserc.json targets the URL https://staging.example.com
lighthouserc.json configures assertions for min category scores or metrics
Produces a valid GitHub Actions YAML workflow configured for push events
The workflow includes installation of @lhci/cli and running 'lhci autorun'

test_prompts.name: before-after-comparison
test_prompts.prompt: Generate a Python script to compare Lighthouse audit scores before and after a change. The script should run audits on two URLs (e.g., staging and production, or a URL before and after a deploy) and output a markdown table showing the diff in category scores and Core Web Vitals.
test_prompts.expected_output: A Python script that performs two audits, compares the resulting JSON outputs, and formats the comparison as a Markdown table.
evaluation_criteria: Produces a valid Python script that can execute or read two reports
Extracts scores for Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO from both runs
Extracts Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, TBT, Speed Index, FID/INP)
Calculates the differences (diffs) for each metric
Generates and prints a cleanly formatted Markdown comparison table

test_prompts.name: authenticated-dashboard-audit
test_prompts.prompt: Our dashboard at https://staging.ourapp.com/dashboard is behind a login page at /login. Username field is id:email, password field is id:password, submit button is id:btn-login. Credentials are testuser@company.com / Test1234!. Write a Python script that logs in first and then runs a Lighthouse audit on the dashboard. Performance must be above 75.
test_prompts.expected_output: A Python script that uses Playwright to authenticate, extracts cookies, passes them to Lighthouse via --extra-headers, audits the dashboard URL, and asserts performance >= 75.
evaluation_criteria: Uses Playwright or Puppeteer to log in and extract cookies
Passes cookies to Lighthouse via --extra-headers
Audits the dashboard URL (https://staging.ourapp.com/dashboard), not the login page
Asserts performance score above 75
Handles the case where login fails (e.g., checks for redirect or cookie presence)

test_prompts.name: cold-warm-user-flow
test_prompts.prompt: Generate a Lighthouse user flow script that audits https://example.com with both a cold load (cache cleared) and a warm load (cache preserved). Output a unified HTML report showing both steps side by side.
test_prompts.expected_output: A Node.js script using Puppeteer and the Lighthouse startFlow API that performs two navigations (cold then warm) and generates a single unified HTML flow report.
evaluation_criteria: Uses Lighthouse startFlow API with Puppeteer
First navigation uses default settings (cold, cache cleared)
Second navigation uses disableStorageReset: true (warm)
Generates a unified HTML flow report (not two separate reports)
Both steps have descriptive stepName labels

test_prompts.name: snapshot-accessibility-audit
test_prompts.prompt: I need to check accessibility on our settings modal. The modal opens when you click the gear icon (id:btn-settings) on /account page. Write a Lighthouse snapshot audit that opens the modal and then checks accessibility score.
test_prompts.expected_output: A Node.js script using Puppeteer and the Lighthouse startFlow API that navigates to /account, clicks the settings button, waits for the modal, and runs flow.snapshot() to check accessibility.
evaluation_criteria: Uses Puppeteer to navigate to /account
Clicks the settings button to open the modal
Waits for modal to be visible before snapshotting
Uses flow.snapshot() not flow.navigate()
Checks accessibility score (not performance, since snapshot mode doesn't measure performance)

test_prompts.name: vague-input-handling
test_prompts.expected_output: Agent asks clarifying questions rather than generating a script from this vague input.
evaluation_criteria: Does NOT generate a script from this vague input
Asks clarifying questions: which URL, desktop or mobile, which categories to check, any authentication needed
Tone is helpful, not dismissive
